claim: Built JavaScript and CSS assets are served with one-year immutable caching.
sandbox: production-format static host; request a hashed asset and assert its HTTP Cache-Control response

claim: The download button reads the latest GitHub release without a browser CORS error and caches a successful response for one hour.
sandbox: mock GitHub Releases API; reload the landing page and assert the asset link renders with one API request

claim: When no release is available, the page explains that downloads are being published and links to GitHub releases.
sandbox: mock a 404 latest-release response and assert the fallback and absence of page errors

claim: The release process produces macOS ARM64 and Intel, Windows MSI and EXE, and Linux AppImage and DEB entries with SHA-256 values.
sandbox: six isolated artifact fixtures; generate latest.json and SHA256SUMS, then compare every entry and digest

claim: The shell installer verifies SHA-256 and refuses a mismatched download before installation.
sandbox: isolated fake download and install directories; exercise mismatch and valid-checksum outcomes

claim: The web demo loads three sample saves, resets them, and removes its separate demo state when starting for real.
sandbox: fresh browser context; use the full sample flow, reset it, leave it, and inspect browser storage

claim: The web sample flow sends no data to a third party.
sandbox: fresh browser context records every request during the complete sample review

claim: The website loads no advertising, analytics, tracking pixels, third-party fonts, or third-party scripts.
sandbox: fresh browser context records landing requests and inspects script, stylesheet, and preload origins

claim: The desktop app loads, reviews, resets, and exits a three-save sample project without choosing a folder.
sandbox: fresh browser app shell completes the sample flow and checks its isolated demo storage

claim: Save work is local and the desktop sample flow sends no save data or telemetry.
where: landing, desktop footer, privacy page, README
sandbox: fresh desktop app shell records all requests during sample scan, bundle review, and reset

claim: A scan does not change source files, recognises 15 save extensions and 11 emulator folders, hashes saves, ignores ROM and BIOS extensions, and skips files over 128 MiB.
sandbox: temporary native folder with every supported extension, every emulator name, ignored files, an exact-limit file, and an oversized file

claim: A .rspbundle is a deflated ZIP containing selected saves and a readable versioned JSON manifest with paths, metadata, and SHA-256 hashes.
sandbox: temporary native source with selected, unselected, and ROM files; read the resulting archive as a consumer

claim: Restore warns about emulator differences and replacements, requires replacement approval, and rejects bad hashes, sizes, paths, duplicates, formats, limits, and escaping symlinks.
sandbox: temporary native bundles and targets cover normal restore, overwrite recovery, tampering, traversal, duplicates, limits, formats, and symlinks

claim: A returned Keeper token is stored locally, removed from the address bar, verified with Sociobot, and its verdict is reused for no more than one day.
where: landing license form, privacy page, README
sandbox: browser storage and recorded verification responses cover URL return, daily cache expiry, and revoked verdict

claim: Keeper stores a reusable device label and up to 100 transfer-history entries on the device.
where: landing Keeper section, desktop Keeper panel, README
sandbox: isolated browser storage saves one device label and 105 transfer entries, then checks the retained latest 100
